subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Asthma symptoms during sports, feeling down lately
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 16 years old, and I'm here because I've been having trouble with my asthma, especially during sports, and I've been feeling really down lately. I was hoping we could talk about it. Doctor: Can you describe the frequency and severity of your asthma symptoms during sports, and what specific medications have you been using to manage them? Patient: Sure, so I have an albuterol inhaler, and I use it whenever I start having trouble. It usually happens during any kind of aerobic workout, like when I'm playing water polo. When it happens, I start feeling like there's phlegm in my throat, my chest gets tight, I wheeze, and I have to sit down or I get lightheaded. The inhaler helps a little, but I still have to stop and catch my breath, and sometimes I get shaky after using it. Doctor: Could you provide more details about the recent feelings of being down, such as how long you've been feeling this way, any specific triggers, and whether you've experienced any changes in sleep, appetite, or interest in activities? Patient: I think the feelings of being down started around when I began this school year. It's mostly because of the stress from my AP classes and SATs. I feel really tired a lot, and I don't really feel like doing anything anymore. My friends go out, but I just want to stay home. I haven't really noticed changes in my sleep or appetite, but I do feel like there's a lot of pressure on me. Doctor: Have you had any recent chest X-rays, pulmonary function tests, or other respiratory evaluations? Patient: No, I haven't had any recent chest X-rays or pulmonary function tests. I just use my inhaler whenever I have an attack, and I haven't been to the doctor for any other respiratory evaluations. Doctor: Have you experienced any changes in your mood or energy
